extracted.intended_audience: readers and writers of poetry and drama; critics and literate public
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and standards for recognising, producing, and critiquing wit (true, mixed, or false) in poetry and the theatre, with attention to character, language, naturalness, and the effects on an audience. Grounded in early-18th-century critical practice as expressed in The Spectator essays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propriety of Thoughts and Words
rubrics_metrics.description: If Wit has truly been defined as a Propriety of Thoughts and Words, then that definition will extend to all sorts of Poetry... Propriety of Thought is that Fancy which arises naturally from the Subject, or which the Poet adapts to it. Propriety of Words is the cloathing of these Thoughts with such Expressions as are naturally proper to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure thoughts spring naturally from the subject (or are well-adapted to it) and clothe those thoughts in expressions that are naturally proper; avoid forced turns of phrase or incongruous diction that break naturalness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truth as the foundation of Thought
rubrics_metrics.description: Truth is the first Quality, and, as it were, the foundation of Thought; the fairest [thoughts] are faultiest if they want this Foundation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base witty thoughts on truth (real insight or plausible observation). While falsehood may sometimes give grace (per some critics), truth remains the primary standard; wit unsupported by truth is fragile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classical Simplicity over Gothick Extravagance
rubrics_metrics.description: These writers... are 'Goths' in Poetry, who, not being able to come up to the beautiful Simplicity of the old Greeks and Romans, have endeavoured to supply its place with all the Extravagancies of an irregular Fancy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor simplicity and classical restraint; avoid piling on extravagant, irregular devices (ornament, novelty for novelty's sake) as substitutes for solid poetic art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid catering to 'Les Petits Esprits' (mob taste)
rubrics_metrics.description: Les Petits Esprits... like nothing but the Husk and Rind of Wit, prefer a Quibble, a Conceit, an Epigram, before solid Sense and elegant Expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not write primarily for readers who prize mere quibbles, conceits, or epigrams; aim instead for solid sense and elegant expression that will reward readers of judgment rather than the mob.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources of Wit: Resemblance and Opposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Not only the Resemblance, but the Opposition of Ideas, does very often produce Wit... I could shew in several little Points, Turns and Antitheses...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use likenesses, contrasts, turns, and antitheses thoughtfully: both resemblance and well-placed opposition are productive strategies for generating wit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reason, Truth, and Nature as measures of Praise/Dispraise
rubrics_metrics.description: I shall always make Reason, Truth, and Nature the Measures of Praise and Dispraise; if those are for me, the Generality of Opinion is of no Consequence against me.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate theatrical and poetic works by their adherence to reason, truth, and nature rather than by prevailing public opinion; praise what accords with these principles and dispraise what violates them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character coherence and plausibility (the 'fine gentleman')
rubrics_metrics.description: I will take for granted, that a fine Gentleman should be honest in his Actions, and refined in his Language... This whole celebrated Piece is a perfect Contradiction to good Manners, good Sense, and common Honesty...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characters' moral behavior, language, and social role should cohere: a 'fine gentleman' ought to display honesty and refined speech; presenting a supposed gentleman as a knave or clown undermines verisimilitude and moral persuasiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate source of comic effect: produce mirth not indignation
rubrics_metrics.description: To speak plainly of this whole Work, I think nothing but being lost to a sense of Innocence and Virtue can make any one see this Comedy, without observing more frequent Occasion to move Sorrow and Indignation, than Mirth and Laughter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In comedy, aim primarily to generate laughter and mirth; if a play more often provokes sorrow or indignation (by rooting humour in the ruin of virtue) it fails as comedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid reliance on mechanical or gamified devices (anagrams, acrosticks, rebuses, puns, chronograms)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Temple... a Regiment of Anagrams... Acrosticks... Chronograms... Rebus's... Crambo... Double Rhymes... Punns... mistaken-identity games produced by identical dress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not make wit chiefly from mechanical word-games, puzzles, double rhymes, or contrivances of mistake-by-costume; such devices belong to 'False Wit' and tend to produce cheap amusement rather than genuine wit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naturalness in gesture and deportment: 'gesture follow thought'
rubrics_metrics.description: The true Art in this Case is, To make the Mind and Body improve together; and if possible, to make Gesture follow Thought, and not let Thought be employed upon Gesture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In performance and social behavior (relevant to actors and 'fine breeding'), ensure physical expression arises from genuine thought and feeling; avoid artificial, taught gestures that draw attention to themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education balance: cultivate mind and body together
rubrics_metrics.description: The general Mistake among us in the Educating our Children, is, That in our Daughters we take care of their Persons and neglect their Minds: in our Sons we are so intent upon adorning their Minds, that we wholly neglect their Bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For performers and those intended for public life, cultivate both intellectual and physical capacities—bodily grace without mind is superficial; mind without deportment is ineffectual.

rubrics_metrics.name: False wit vanishes before Truth
rubrics_metrics.description: As the dazling Light, which flowed from TRUTH, began to shine upon her, [the Goddess of FALSEHOOD] faded insensibly... the whole Army that attended her... shrunk into Nothing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sincerity, clarity, and truthfulness expose and dissolve contrived or deceptive cleverness; prefer straightforward truth over elaborate false devices when seeking enduring wit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid making novelty an end in itself
rubrics_metrics.description: He borrows all from a greater Master in his own Profession, and, which is worse, improves nothing which he finds: Nature fails him, and being forced to his old Shift, he has Recourse to Witticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not borrow superficially from superior models or rely on novelty without understanding or improvement; if natural talent or insight is lacking, mere wit will not substitute for genuine artistic worth.
